-- /home/altjoe/projects/opencode-manage/db/migrations/0002_work_items.up.sql FINAL
-- Goals/Milestones Go-core: canonical work-item state, directory-scoped in
-- the global manage.db. Supersedes the provisional Lua/TS state.db adapters.
CREATE TABLE work_items (
    id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    directory       TEXT    NOT NULL,
    parent_id       INTEGER REFERENCES work_items(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    kind            TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('goal', 'milestone')),
    name            TEXT    NOT NULL,
    description     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    status          TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'planned',
    importance      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 3,
    sibling_order   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    hold_reason     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    deferred_reason TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    merged_into_id  INTEGER REFERENCES work_items(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    created_at      TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    updated_at      TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    completed_at    TEXT
);

CREATE INDEX idx_work_items_dir_parent ON work_items (directory, parent_id, sibling_order, id);
CREATE INDEX idx_work_items_dir_status ON work_items (directory, status, importance, sibling_order);

CREATE TABLE active_work_item (
    directory  TEXT    PRIMARY KEY,
    item_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES work_items(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    updated_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);

CREATE TABLE work_item_events (
    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    directory  TEXT    NOT NULL,
    item_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES work_items(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    created_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    actor      TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'user',
    event_type TEXT    NOT NULL,
    reason     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    session_id TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT ''
);

CREATE INDEX idx_wi_events_dir_item ON work_item_events (directory, item_id, created_at DESC);

CREATE TABLE work_item_suggestions (
    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    created_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    session_id TEXT    NOT NULL,
    directory  TEXT    NOT NULL,
    item_id    INTEGER REFERENCES work_items(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    action     TEXT    NOT NULL,
    payload    TEXT    NOT NULL,
    rationale  TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    status     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
    applied_at TEXT,
    applied_by TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'user'
);

CREATE INDEX idx_wi_suggestions_dir_status ON work_item_suggestions (directory, status);

-- /home/altjoe/projects/opencode-manage/db/queries/work_items.sql FINAL
-- name: ListWorkItems :many
SELECT * FROM work_items
WHERE directory = sqlc.arg(directory)
ORDER BY parent_id IS NOT NULL, parent_id, sibling_order, id;

-- name: GetWorkItem :one
SELECT * FROM work_items
WHERE id = sqlc.arg(id) AND directory = sqlc.arg(directory);

-- name: ListSiblings :many
SELECT * FROM work_items
WHERE directory = sqlc.arg(directory)
  AND (parent_id = sqlc.arg(parent_id) OR (parent_id IS NULL AND sqlc.arg(parent_id) IS NULL))
ORDER BY sibling_order, id;

-- name: InsertWorkItem :one
INSERT INTO work_items (directory, parent_id, kind, name, description, importance, sibling_order)
VALUES (sqlc.arg(directory), sqlc.arg(parent_id), sqlc.arg(kind), sqlc.arg(name), sqlc.arg(description), sqlc.arg(importance), sqlc.arg(sibling_order))
RETURNING *;

-- name: UpdateWorkItem :exec
UPDATE work_items
SET name = sqlc.arg(name), description = sqlc.arg(description), updated_at = datetime('now')
WHERE id = sqlc.arg(id) AND directory = sqlc.arg(directory);

-- name: SetWorkItemStatus :exec
UPDATE work_items
SET status = sqlc.arg(status), hold_reason = sqlc.arg(hold_reason),
    completed_at = CASE WHEN sqlc.arg(status) = 'completed' THEN datetime('now') ELSE NULL END,
    updated_at = datetime('now')
WHERE id = sqlc.arg(id) AND directory = sqlc.arg(directory);

-- name: SetWorkItemImportance :exec
UPDATE work_items
SET importance = sqlc.arg(importance), updated_at = datetime('now')
WHERE id = sqlc.arg(id) AND directory = sqlc.arg(directory);

-- name: SetWorkItemParentOrder :exec
UPDATE work_items
SET parent_id = sqlc.arg(parent_id), sibling_order = sqlc.arg(sibling_order), updated_at = datetime('now')
WHERE id = sqlc.arg(id) AND directory = sqlc.arg(directory);

-- name: ShiftSiblingOrders :exec
UPDATE work_items
SET sibling_order = sibling_order + 1, updated_at = datetime('now')
WHERE directory = sqlc.arg(directory)
  AND (parent_id = sqlc.arg(parent_id) OR (parent_id IS NULL AND sqlc.arg(parent_id) IS NULL))
  AND sibling_order >= sqlc.arg(min_order);

-- name: SetSiblingOrder :exec
UPDATE work_items
SET sibling_order = sqlc.arg(sibling_order), updated_at = datetime('now')
WHERE id = sqlc.arg(id) AND directory = sqlc.arg(directory);

-- name: UpsertActiveWorkItem :exec
INSERT INTO active_work_item (directory, item_id)
VALUES (sqlc.arg(directory), sqlc.arg(item_id))
ON CONFLICT(directory) DO UPDATE SET item_id = excluded.item_id, updated_at = datetime('now');

-- name: ClearActiveWorkItem :exec
DELETE FROM active_work_item WHERE directory = sqlc.arg(directory);

-- name: GetActiveWorkItem :one
SELECT * FROM active_work_item WHERE directory = sqlc.arg(directory);

-- name: InsertWorkItemEvent :exec
INSERT INTO work_item_events (directory, item_id, actor, event_type, reason, session_id)
VALUES (sqlc.arg(directory), sqlc.arg(item_id), sqlc.arg(actor), sqlc.arg(event_type), sqlc.arg(reason), sqlc.arg(session_id));

-- name: ListWorkItemEvents :many
SELECT * FROM work_item_events
WHERE directory = sqlc.arg(directory) AND item_id = sqlc.arg(item_id)
ORDER BY id DESC;

-- name: AppendSuggestion :one
INSERT INTO work_item_suggestions (session_id, directory, item_id, action, payload, rationale)
VALUES (sqlc.arg(session_id), sqlc.arg(directory), sqlc.arg(item_id), sqlc.arg(action), sqlc.arg(payload), sqlc.arg(rationale))
RETURNING *;

-- name: ListSuggestions :many
SELECT * FROM work_item_suggestions
WHERE directory = sqlc.arg(directory) AND status = sqlc.arg(status)
ORDER BY id;

-- name: GetSuggestion :one
SELECT * FROM work_item_suggestions
WHERE id = sqlc.arg(id) AND directory = sqlc.arg(directory);

-- name: SetSuggestionStatus :exec
UPDATE work_item_suggestions
SET status = sqlc.arg(status),
    applied_at = CASE WHEN sqlc.arg(status) = 'applied' THEN datetime('now') ELSE NULL END,
    applied_by = sqlc.arg(applied_by)
WHERE id = sqlc.arg(id) AND directory = sqlc.arg(directory);

content:
---
name: user-commands
description: "Command delivery and information-request conventions for the manage plugin: the assistant has no shell permissions, so every command it needs executed must be handed to the user as a copy-paste-ready bash block (cd to absolute path + one command per line), and missing information must be requested via the user's standard commands — never assumed absent. Use when supplying commands to run, asking the user for grep/build/test/git output, or after proposal verdicts."
---

# User-Command Delivery & Information Requests

The assistant has **no shell permissions**. It can never run grep, make, go,
sqlc, git, or any command itself. Every command the assistant needs executed
must be handed to the user as a ready-to-run block. This is not optional — the
assistant will never gain shell access, so the user is the execution channel.

## Command delivery format (mandatory)

When supplying commands for the user to run, use ONE fenced bash block:

```bash
cd /abs/path/to/project
make sqlc
make test
```

Rules:
- First line is always `cd <absolute-path>` so the block works from any shell
  location. The user must not have to know which directory to run from.
- One command per line. Nothing else inside the fence.
- Never inline commands in prose (`` `make sqlc` `` inside a sentence), never
  embed them in numbered steps with arrows or dashes. The user must be able to
  select the whole block and paste without editing ("no surgery").

## Never assume absence

If information is not in context and the assistant cannot access it (no shell),
it must **NOT** conclude the information doesn't exist. It must ask the user to
run the standard command and paste the output. Examples:
- grep results → ask the user to run the grep and paste the output
- build/test output → ask the user to run make and paste the failure
- git state → ask the user to run git status/log and paste
- file contents → ask the user to open/read the file and paste what matters

## Standard commands by circumstance

Use the user's standard commands, not invented ones:

| Circumstance | Command |
|---|---|
| sqlc generation | `make sqlc` |
| tests | `make test` |
| build | `make build` |
| run daemon | `make run` |
| go mod tidy | `make tidy` |
| migration down | `make migrate-down` |
| SQL diagnostics | give the raw query to run |
| logs | ask the user to check the logs — they contain the error |

When unsure which command the user prefers for a circumstance, **ASK** — do not
invent a command or a flag.

## Verdict-driven follow-up commands

After the user accepts/rejects proposals (verdicts), supply the follow-up
commands automatically based on what changed:
- Accepted Go/sqlc changes → `make sqlc` then `make test` then `make build`
- Accepted migration → restart the daemon (it runs migrations on start)
- Accepted TS plugin changes → no build step (hotreload)
- Rejected changes → no commands needed

## Context gate

When context is missing (a file, a decision, a command preference), ask for it
explicitly. Never guess, never drift, never assume absence.
